I’ve been living with my childhood best friend, and we keep circling back to the young girls we once were.

We played outside like our lives depended on it,

Gulping down entire glass of water in the 10 second pause when mummy would call you amidst running like crazy.
Playing until the very last ounce of energy. There was no concept for "feeling tired".
Bruised knees, fights, nothing could stop us.

Playing wasn’t actually an activity; it was a really really important part of the routing like sleeping eating and breathing.

We talked about how growing up in a girls’ school shaped us differently. 

I remember genuinely believing I COULD DO ANYTHING A BOY CAN DO.
If strength was needed, I’d train. 
If skill was needed, I’d learn. There was no quiet doubt sitting in the corner of my mind.

There was NO idea of COMPARISON WITH the other [ORGANIZATION] because it just didn't exist around.

Equality or FEMINISM were NOT ideas or concepts we were taught, 
These were normal natural behaviours.

Surrounded only by girls, we never felt lesser or separate. We were told, and more importantly shown, that wanting something was reason enough to go after it.

Losing wasn’t in our vocabulary. Feeling weak didn’t exist.

But now, after stepping out into the world, 

after reading headlines, hearing stories, living a little, 
I feel reality press its weight on me.

The realization that without any training, without effort, a man can still HURT me.

Wo [PERSON] [PERSON].
He can leave a mark I may never fully recover from.

That truth makes me feel weak in a way I never had language for before. It makes the little girl in me quietly go sad.

I know I can still train. I can build strength, resilience, awareness.
But I can’t unsee the truth.

The same people who once taught me to be strong now teach me to be safe.

Growing up there were days.

I used to get irritated when my mother worried about my safety.
It felt excessive, unnecessary, like fear borrowed from a world I didn’t live in.

I don’t remember when I stopped arguing.

One day, I just understood.
And that contrast.
that’s all this is.
Something I’ve recently learned to notice.

interviewed for a Product Ops role  it was a newly launched team at the company.

I gave 2 small interviews the first day.

Next day  a 45–50 minute discussion on the specific role.
( I noticed I got marked good for communication but bad on product knowledge side)

Moved to the final round.

Then came this really simple question:
“What do you mean by cloud?”

I said cloud computing removes the need for users to manage physical hardware for storing data.
Which... isn’t wrong.
But it’s also not complete.
What I didn’t say,  even though I knew it, were words like servers, data centers, distributed infrastructure.

I know about how AI data centers cause threats to climate. ( Got spiralled in that thought process at that very moment)

I know data doesn’t float in the air.
I know it’s stored, processed, replicated across huge server farms.
All of that was in my head.
Just not on my tongue.

The Director smiled and said,
“So... data just exists in the air?”
And instead of immediately correcting myself, I said yes.

LIKE A FOOL.
Rest of the interview went well, I gave answers.
It was hardly 15 minutes.

That one second really mattered.
I got rejected later on.

Later, when I asked for feedback from a senior at the same company.

What is your take on luxury items or on a more decent level, ' branded items'?

Branded things are expensive because they promise quality.
Luxury items are expensive on a whole different scale - far beyond material or utility.

Normally, Selling price  of a product= Cost ( material cost+ making cost) + brand value 

I wondered however expensive the parts of a watch can be, what makes it final prize so freaking high.

For luxury items, the brand value crosses a whole new horizon.

Questioning about this stuff made me read about the "Veblen Effect".
It’s basically when the price is the product.

People are buying luxury items not just for use but for a social positioning.

-The more expensive something is,
the fewer people can touch it.
-And the fewer people who can touch it,
the more powerful it feels to own.

My mind just hadn’t learned how to hold emotions gently.
